item.intervention: Addition of Hafnium (Hf) to create a quinary W-Ta-Cr-V-Hf alloy
item.processing: Magnetron-sputtering deposition from metal targets at room temperature, 3 mTorr pressure, no bias voltage
item.test_conditions: In situ TEM annealing at 1173 K; 16 keV He implantation; dual-beam irradiation (1 MeV Kr+ + 16 keV He+) at 1173 K
item.structure_change: Grain refinement occurred during dual-beam irradiation (average grain size dropped to 21.1 ± 1.4 nm), whereas He implantation caused grain growth to 36.3 ± 1.8 nm; no detectable grain growth under dual-beam conditions compared to annealed state
item.property_change: Grain size decreased from 26.3 ± 1.1 nm (annealed) to 21.1 ± 1.4 nm (dual-beam irradiated); no dislocation loop formation detected after 8.5 dpa
item.attributed_mechanism: Grain refinement caused by cascade effect where overlapping cascades smaller than grain size fragment grains; high density of stable grain boundaries and chemical complexity altering defect recombination rates
quotes: However, during the dual-beam irradiation, grain refinement occurred, and the average grain size dropped to 21.1 ± 1.4 nm after a total irradiation time of ~94 mins.
Dislocation loops were not detected even after 8.5 dpa and at 9.13% He implantation during the dual-beam experiment.
This suggests that such a grain refinement observed in the dual-beam irradiation case was caused by a cascade effect.

item.intervention: Replacement of V with Fe (attempted), then addition of Hf to W-Ta-Cr-V
item.processing: CALPHAD calculations and thermophysical parameter calculations (ΔH_mix, ΔS_mix, δ, Ω, VEC)
item.test_conditions: Computational modeling of phase stability and morphology
item.structure_change: Fe addition promoted undesired intermetallic phases and lowered melting point; Hf addition favored single-phase BCC HEA formation with VEC value of 5.2
item.property_change: Not stated (computational prediction of phase stability)
item.attributed_mechanism: Group IV elements (Hf) used to lower VEC value below 4.4 to enhance stability; Hf selected for high melting point to avoid high activation
quotes: However, the addition of Fe in both low and high elemental concentrations promotes the formation of several undesired intermetallic phases instead of single-phase solid-solution, as well as lowering the melting point of the system.
Group IV elements can then be used to pursue this approach (e.g., Ti, Zr, and Hf) and modify the W-Ta-Cr-V RHEA.
In this case, 5.2 was shown to be the minimum achievable VEC value, and certain compositions were shown to favor the formation of a single-phase BCC HEA.

item.base_system: W 29.4 Ta 42 Cr 5.0 V 16.1 Hf 7.5 thin film (as-deposited)
item.intervention: In situ TEM annealing at 1173 K for ~30 mins
item.structure_change: Grain size increased from 24.5 ± 1.3 nm to 26.3 ± 1.1 nm; Hf segregates to grain boundaries; V and Cr inhomogeneously distributed
item.property_change: Hardness increased from 13.25 GPa to 16.25 GPa
item.attributed_mechanism: Increase in hardness after annealing is solely associated with Hf segregation along the GBs
quotes: After annealing to 1173 K for ~30 mins in the TEM, the grain size increased to 26.3 ± 1.1 nm.

Careful analysis of the elemental maps revealed that after annealing, Hf segregates to grain boundaries, and V and Cr are also inhomogeneously distributed throughout the sample, thus indicating segregation.
The increase in hardness after annealing was ~3 GPa and this can be directly attributed to Hf segregation to grain boundaries as revealed in Fig. 2 and in the STEM-EDX mapping as insets in Fig. 5.

item.base_system: W 31 Ta 34 Cr 5.0 V 27 Hf 3.0 alloy
item.intervention: Thermal modeling of chemical short-range order (SRO) and order-disorder transition temperature (ODTT)
item.processing: Cluster Expansion (CE) and Monte Carlo calculations on 16,000 atom simulation cells
item.structure_change: Cr-Hf precipitate visible at 300 K but vanishes at 620 K; ODTT of ~1120 K predicted
item.property_change: Not stated (predictive modeling of phase stability)
item.attributed_mechanism: Negative SRO indicates ordering and tendency to form intermetallic compounds; homogenization occurs when SRO values tend to zero marking ODTT
quotes: Among the considered pairs of atoms, the strongest attraction is observed for the Cr-Hf pair, which presents the most negative SRO parameter at low temperatures for both RHEAs.
The W 31 Ta 34 Cr 5 V 27 Hf 3.0 showed an ODTT of ~1120 K which roughly coincides with the irradiation temperature.
Homogenization of the elements occurs when all SRO values tend to zero which marks the ODTT of the alloy.

item.property_change: Total change in volume ~0.3% after 8.45 dpa; no loop formation
